title: Model ingest metadata contract, soft-pin clarity, and rollback playbook
creator: Nora Kim
description:
Summary:
We need a concise, operational ingest metadata contract and a 'soft-pin' guidance that product, runtime, and onboarding engineers can use to decide if a new open model variant can be admitted without hard version pinning. This ticket clarifies acceptance criteria, document scope, and rollback triggers for experimental/ephemeral open model submissions.

Problem context:
- Teams continue to onboard community weights that differ in tokenizer, kv-cache layout, and optional fused ops. Runtime teams currently triage each ingest manually; that creates 48–72h delays and inconsistent decisions between catalog reviewers. Lack of a clear soft-pin contract causes either overly conservative hard-pinning (higher operational burden) or unsafe unpinned admissions (runtime failures, customer incidents).

Goals (what success looks like):
- A one-page ingest metadata contract template that intake reviewers can require for any open model variant.
- A 'soft-pin' semantics doc describing when we allow runtime to accept variant without strict pin (e.g., minor tokenizer differences, optional attention optimizations) and when hard pin is mandatory.
- A set of automated and manual rollback triggers tied to runtime metrics, acceptance tests, and customer-reported regressions.
- Clear responsibilities workflow between PM, Runtime/ENG, Design (if output changes), and Support.

Scope clarifications (in vs out):
- In: metadata fields (tokenizer id, model/weights SHA, expected seq-lens, kv-cache layout, fused op flags), compatibility note examples, soft-pin rationale template, and rollback criteria. Also define triage SLA and required artifacts (eval prompts, small perf profile).
- Out: building full automated runtime compatibility verification tooling (separate ENG epic), rolling out soft-pin for dedicated/private customers (follow-on privacy/regulatory checks).

Trade-offs considered:
- Tight metadata schema vs. low-friction onboarding: We propose a minimal required contract + optional extended fields. Required fields must be present or intake is blocked. This preserves speed while raising the floor on signal.
- Soft-pin vs. no-pin: soft-pin allows faster discovery of useful variants while bounding risk via explicit rollback triggers and canary traffic rules. The risk is increased variance in client experience; mitigations include restricted default routing and automated sanity probes.

Acceptance criteria (see list below):
- Intake template exists in Confluence and is referenced by onboarding form.
- Runtime has documented 'allowed compat deltas' list and an automated sanity probe (smoke inference) is run pre-acceptance by ENG.
- Rollback playbook defined with metric thresholds and a pager path.

Deliverables:
- Confluence page: ingest-metadata-contract + soft-pin guidance (single page with examples).
- Short PRD summarizing policy and expected changes to onboarding UI.
- Updated onboarding form (link included) requiring minimal metadata fields.
- Rollback playbook artifact and runbook for on-call.

Notes on rollout plan:
1) Phase 1 (internal beta): pilot on catalog experimental channel with 5 community models for 2 weeks. Traffic limited to 5% by routing policy. Validate automated sanity probes and latency/cost baselines.
2) Phase 2 (expanded pilot): widen to 20% traffic and two additional models. Collect evals and customer feedback.
3) Full adoption: after 4 weeks of stable pilot metrics, update public onboarding flow and catalog labeling.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence ingest-metadata-contract page published with template and examples
Onboarding intake form enforces required metadata fields and blocks submissions missing them
Runtime team runs automated smoke inference during intake and documents probe results in intake ticket
Soft-pin policy defines at minimum: allowed tokenizer deltas, allowed fused-op flags, and disallowed runtime-breaking deltas
Canary routing and 5% traffic cap configured for all soft-pinned variants during first 14 days
Rollback playbook lists metric thresholds (error rate + latency + correctness regression) and an on-call pager flow
decisions: Require minimal metadata: tokenizer_id, weights_sha256, expected_max_seq, kv_layout_hint, fused_ops: list
Soft-pin allowed when only tokenizer tokenization mapping differs or fused ops are optional (no structural kv cache change)
Any change to kv-cache layout or model compilation ABI requires hard pin until runtime validation passes
Pilot gating uses canary traffic + automated eval suite; pilot length 14 days by default
tasks: Create Confluence page and ingest template (owner: PM)
Add required fields to onboarding form (ownership: Developer Experience)
ENG to implement pre-acceptance smoke inference probe and document results (owner: Runtime)
Define canary routing defaults and set 5% traffic cap for soft-pinned variants (owner: Routing)
Draft rollback runbook and pager playbook (owner: SRE)
Coordinate internal beta cohort and run pilot signals collection (owner: PM + Runtime)
Write acceptance tests and ensure onboarding form blocks incomplete submissions (owner: QA)
